utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. And good afternoon to you, sir. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Before I begin my questioning I wanted to indicate that the exhibits that were used by my friend yesterday and that had been admitted into evidence ranging from 2D94 to 2D99 were actually photographs that were magnified and they were taken by a member of the Prosecution, Office of the Prosecutor. Unfortunately, at this stage, we are not able to provide the Court with the level of magnification of those photographs as that person is away from the office, but when he returns in a couple of weeks' time, we would able to provide that information to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you continue, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. In reference with the objection of my colleague I would like to emphasize that some of the photographs are visibly magnified and some are not and we have no proof nor confirmation about it and we received those photographs from the Prosecution and we don't know if they have been magnified as my colleague just said. I would just like to say that on the photograph 2D88, the cliff is visible. The cliff where that photo was taken from. So I doubt that this photograph has been magnified as my colleague just said. If it had been zoomed, then the cliff would have -- wouldn't have been as visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. I don't believe there was any objection taken. We were merely being informed so that we were not misled. And frankly, I don't think it is of any significance whether the photograph is magnified or not. The photographic image is very small compared to the natural size, in any event. The magnification is merely an aid to seeing what is in parts of the photograph, as long as the whole photograph is magnified there is no distortion of perspective. Thank you. Please continue, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, good afternoon, Witness. I would just like to clarify a few points with you, sir. Just as a point of clarification, as a reservist you indicated that you were attached to the 1st Infantry Company of the 3rd Guardist Battalion, is that correct, in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. From the 1st Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you said that your immediate superior was Mario Jurisic who was the commander of the 1st Company, but you also referred to a Lieutenant Brasnarski. And I just wanted to clarify with you who is it that you received orders from or who you answer to? Was it Mario Jurisic or Brasnarski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if a superior officer is on the position and I'm on the same position and if that person has a higher rank than me, then that is the commander of our unit, whether it was Mario, whether Mario was present or not, he was in charge of the position. I think I explained very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But just so that we're clear, Witness, Lieutenant Brasnarski was in fact the deputy of the 1st Infantry Company and Mario Jurisic was the commander of that company. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And as you mentioned, the commander of the battalion was Major Mitre Despodov. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I'd just now like to deal briefly with the training that you received prior to taking up your post in August 2001 on Smok, and you mentioned that in mid-June, you went to the military barracks of Ilinden and one day you were introduced to weapons where you received training in firing. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I said. During the training and the weapons that we were charged with, we had to handle that weapons, and therefore we needed to know better that weapons because a long time has passed since I served army and things get forgotten. So that was the training and we had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. But you mentioned, I believe, sir, yesterday, and this is what I'd like to clarify, that you were trained at firing weapons for one day. So were you trained at firing weapons for one day or was it a longer period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that from the times of the Yugoslavia National Army the infantry training that was conducted in JNA, one can become a member of the infantry only after completing a six-month training, and that is where I received my rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it is that you received some additional training for one day when you returned in mid-June. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was just firing, shooting, just to get to know the weapons that we were going use. Your Honours, I was charged with an automatic rifle, and I explained it well, and the machine-gun, according to the law, since I had a rank of lance corporal, only a person that had been trained can use machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A person that has a rank of lance corporal need to know the machine-gun and even train other people to use it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us, sir, what types of weapons were you trained on at that time in June or August 2001? What weapons were you using?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was an automatic rifle. It is a fact. I said that. That is the weapons that we used, the sniper, the machine-gun that was stationed on the point. It was not returned in the barracks. But every trained person that joins the army can use that machine-gun together with tactic training on the point where we were. I could train five persons in one day. Your Honours, that is what I wanted to say. That is the answer to the question which weapons we used.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say that you had -- you used an automatic rifle, was that an AK-47?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kalashnikov.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And would you agree with me, sir, that a Kalashnikov has an effective range of about 500 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How much did you say? 100 metres. What do you mean 500 metres? You know, we know what is the range of an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, sir, just to clarify, I'm asking: Is the range for this automatic rifle, the AK-47, 500 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 300 and 400 metres of range. And that is the most precise answer to you, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I interrupt to inquire what you mean by range. I think you may find a single round fired from that weapon will travel much more than 500 metres. The question is how accurately it will fire at three or four or 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and I think that -- I'll clarify that. I think that is why I was using the term "effective."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And I think the witness is telling you that once you get above 400, he is not too confident of hitting anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can you indicate, sir, that the sniper that you were using in your unit, what is the range for that, or the effective range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Range of a sniper, hmm. That is a good question. You want a definition? What is the effective range? Is that what you want from me?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Let me ask you this first, sir. What kind of sniper were you using. You said you had one sniper when you were up at Smok. What kind of sniper were you using?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Calibre 7, 9. [In English] Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And how far would you be able to accurately fire with that calibre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be precise, 300 to 400 metres, not more. Well, it can have a range of 5.000 metres, but without any precision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps just moving on to something else, sir. How many men in your unit were with you between 10 and 12 August at Smok?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said previously, Your Honours, on the position of Smok, I had five soldiers. Those five soldiers were always on that position, changing into shifts. One shift was 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And were they all reservists like yourself, those five soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With exception, whenever need arose, we had a higher officer. If there were combat activities on the positions and if the superior was of higher rank, then that superior was in charge of that unit or that company.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you said -- you mentioned also, sir, that you were using binoculars at the time. What level of magnification were you using to make your observations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall quite precisely, because my eyesight was much better at the time. I said that I now have problems with the eyesight. I'm a bit disabled because I'm using welding equipment which harmed my sight. I said that on the position of Smok we used binoculars and the sniper sight, but what was the magnification, you know, a person can see well 200 metres away if that person has good eyesight. But you can see the flames and the fire that one gun releases so it is easy to see it even with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I guess the answer to my question then is you can't remember the level of magnification of the binoculars you were using at the time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I wanted to see further away I had to adjust the magnification to a higher level. I said I cannot really recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I think you have answered my question. But I take it, then, you -- can you recall, then, the magnification on the sniper that you were using, the sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm, I cannot really recall. I don't remember whether I had to adjust it to three circles or four circles, depending on the object that I wanted to see and how far that object was. I really cannot be precise in millimetres. I'm not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, you testified yesterday, I believe, that on the 10th of August, 2001, that Commander Brasnarski called you - he was the deputy in your -- in your company - and told you or instructed you to observe attentively in case there were terrorists moving within the village of Ljuboten. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So your job, one of your main functions when you were up at Smok, was to observe all movements within the village and report your observations back to the command. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. I think your question is a bit different. My task after the soldiers had been killed, because we have to divide these two things, I said that very precisely yesterday. If Brasnarski was on the position because he had a higher rank than me, he was my commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I want to interrupt you for a moment because I think you have misunderstood my question. I'm not asking who your commander is, okay? I'm just asking you that one of your main tasks as you were -- the order that you were given on that day was to make observations of the movements that occurred within the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my position, to observe the village from the higher part of the mountain. Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Once you made those observations, if you were to see any type of movements, such as firing or terrorist movement or anything that was important, you would report those observations to the command and that might be to Mario Jurisic or Brasnarski or whoever your commander was at the time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think we are misunderstanding each other, Your Honours. I would like to explain. If an officer has a higher rank and that officer is my superior, he informs to the commanding post, he is the commander of that unit or company, and he is responsible about the information that he gives to the commanding post. I had a very low rank. I couldn't give them any information. The commanding was done like this: If the officer had a higher rank, then he was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So let's start with the 10th of August, sir. If you made an observation on the 10th of, for example, firing -- firing from the village on the 10th, who would you report that to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please again explain this question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Suppose you had made an observation on the 10th of a movement in the village or a firing from somewhere in the village, who would you report that observation to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander heard the shooting. When our soldiers were killed, because we are talking about that day, our soldiers hit a land-mine up there in Bacila and --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But that's not what I'm asking you, sir. I'm asking if you made an observation that the commander may or may not have heard, who would you report to on the 10th? Who was your commander at the time that you reported to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understood the question. To my commander, to my superior, to Mario Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you had made an observation that was important on the 12th of August, just so that we're absolutely clear about this, sir, then you would also report that observation to Mario Jurisic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was on the position, then you always report to the commander that is on your position. The commander functions as a commander and forwards the information to the higher commanders. That is what I can say, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who was the commander on your position on the 10th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Mario Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Mario Jurisic was our commander and he was the army commander. He was active army officer. He wasn't a reservist.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Who was the highest ranking officer at your position on Smok on that day? Who was present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the position was Brasnarski.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So if something -- if you had seen something that was important that was happening in the village, you would report to Brasnarski on that day, on the 10th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In given moments, yes. If I'm at the position and if I -- since there was a limitation on the talks about that day, if the commander was on the next position, he tells us that he will send a courier in the trench and he will inform us. Otherwise, it is not possible to inform each other or to report to each other. This was how things were at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And so on the 10th, if something important happened in the village, you would report to Commander Brasnarski, who was at Smok with you, and then Commander Brasnarski may report back to the command about what was happening in the village. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he is nearby, and as I mentioned several times he was at the Bomba position, he gives all information where necessary. In the command, in the headquarters or further up, this is a procedure which they have, a command procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned, sir, that the mode of communication that was being used at those positions was a wire telephone, and that is how observations, whether it was done by you or by the commander, were reported back to the command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have a courier or a duty officer on the phone, at given moments from the five soldiers which I have at my disposal on a shift, in an hour or two hours' time, we took turns from the position and one of these -- one person was always on duty on the telephone. It may have been me or another soldier. The person who was on duty with the telephone that he communicates with the commander, Brasnarski or vice versa, depending on the day. This was how the communication went.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the person who was on duty on the telephone, sir, regardless of who it was, was required to maintain constant communication with the command of the 1st Infantry Company during that critical time and -- so that the observations would continuously be reported back to the command. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command cannot be informed all the time. I said this twice. If a commander is at a neighbouring point, a commander of a superior rank, then we would be in communication with them, or a courier would run over to that position, or his courier would come to us and then it was he that communicates this further. This is what I can respond to your question about how the communication went.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But the point is, sir, that whether or not the commander was at the position, or a courier, or somebody was on the telephone reporting the observations to the -- to the command, the point was that the important observations were being reported on a regular basis constantly back to the command, so that the command can issue the required orders. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot fabricate things --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I'm just asking you to just answer my questions as I ask them. Thank you. So would it be fair to say, sir, that when -- each time that a target was observed by someone such as yourself, or perhaps Commander Brasnarski or whomever was present at the time, or saw firing towards your positions, that was reported back to the command. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I answered this question, and I think I did so realistically from my point of view. If the commander, a superior with a higher rank, is on that position or not, regardless of this, we call him or we inform him and he informs the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command calls into the command centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And all targets or firing that was occurring from the village towards your positions was ultimately being reported to the command centre, whether it was done by the commander or somebody else. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we can clarify this now. I tell you very precisely, at the Smok position, there were five people and there's a commander, so-and-so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think you understand my question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the end of the shift.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't think you understand what I'm asking. I'm going to rephrase my question. That might be my fault. Whether it was the commander -- I see that my friend, Your Honour, is on his feet, so I may just stop there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting, Your Honours, but I think the witness has been answering these questions several times now, and I think it's not a good form that this question continues to be asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. There is a lack of communication between the witness and Ms. Issa, which is probably nobody's fault, the fact of is that the precise point that Ms. Issa is trying to get clarified is escaping the witness and he is answering other matters. Just how long Ms. Issa will keep at it, we will find out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Hopefully not too long, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to try to ask you this as precisely as I can and I would ask to you please listen very carefully to the precise question that I'm asking you and only to answer that question, okay? Regardless of whether the information or the observations that was being relayed to the command centre was done by the commander at Smok or by yourself or your colleagues, my question is that all observations, all -- all of targets or firing that occurred within the village towards your positions was reported back to the command centre. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're coming back to this again, about what I'm supposed to be giving as an answer. For example, when I was on duty with five people, I, as the commander, have to make notes and to give them over to the next day's shift, to tell them what had happened. My commander will come. I write the notes in a notebook. Am I clear in what I'm saying? I write this down in a notebook. And when the new shift comes, the new commander writes what he had noted, whether there had been firing and whatnot, and the commander takes these to the command post. I hope I'm clear about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So the effect of that, then, sir, is that all observations of firing were supposed to be noted, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course and correct. And we informed the commander and he knows about what was going on. This is what I have been answering.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a precise manner, I have been trying to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir. And after the -- a target or a location of -- or after -- something was observed, where somebody was -- had been firing at your positions and that was reported back to the command centre, or the commander, depending on who you were dealing with at the time, you would then receive an order to fire back at that specific target, either you or your colleagues. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said if there's a commander there, if there's a superior there and we see that we're being fired at, then this is quite normal. The commander is in command. This was exactly what I was saying. The commanders are those in charge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. And once you've fired at that target, assuming that there is no commander there and the target was neutralized, you would report that fact, that the target was neutralized to the commander, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm attacked --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if there was a commander there that was present - for example, Commander Brasnarski, if I'm pronouncing that properly - he may report that or he would report that back to the command centre, that fact that a target was neutralized. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is the one who decides, be it destroyed or not. He is the one who tells on. I cannot tell you offhand about certain things which I do not know about.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Constant communication, sir, was important with the command centre and/or your immediate commanders, because the command needed to have the most up-to-the-minute information at that critical time in order to issue orders on the ground. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander who is, at that point, it depends on whether he can convey this, and if it is possible, he is the one who will do it. I can't say this. I cannot say anything to the command centre. The commander, if he has the need or if there are certain activities then he --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I just want to clarify a few points just moving on to a slightly different topic? You mentioned, sir, that you saw at one stage on the 12th of August, 2001, Macedonian security forces walking behind a Hermelin. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, when you say "Macedonian security forces," you mean the police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I have to tell you precisely. Macedonian forces are all security forces, without limitations. We are the army, army for security of Macedonia. Security forces --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm going to stop you there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- depending on the sector experts will tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What you saw on the 12th of August were police officers or members of the police in the village. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw I already told.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a concrete answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm asking you now to answer a more precise question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Security forces, do you understand me? I saw security forces at the Ljuboten place. Security forces, when I say this, this can mean in the police sector or other areas about which I cannot tell you in an expert manner. I don't know who this was and how this was. These were our security forces. This is the point I made yesterday and today. I hope I have been clear. This is what I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, the army never entered the village that day, village of Ljuboten, on the 12th of August, did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to reply to this. From my position, no soldier -- none of my soldiers went anywhere, not to the village, not anywhere. As for who entered the village, how they entered the village, I can't know about these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just as a point of clarification, sir, you mentioned yesterday that you spent the whole day, Saturday, at the funeral, and you said something about being in the dining-room of the village of Ljuboten. And I just want to clarify the record. When you say you spent the day in the dining-room, you mean Ljubanci. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Yes, this is what I said. We're Christians and when someone dies, a parent, mother, father --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I understand I just wanted to clarify the location where you were, to correct the transcript. Just moving on to a different topic. Ljuboten is quite a densely built-up town, isn't it. It is very dense and the houses are built very close together. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends. There is Staro Maalo, there is Novo Maalo. Now the houses are built in a more modern fashion. The old houses were more densely placed together. The new houses are somewhat different. I can't tell you know what the village looks like.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm asking you what the village looked like in August 2001. The houses were built up very close together and it is quite a densely built town. We can look at a photograph, if you like. But isn't that how it was built in 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. Houses are one next to each other. In some areas. For example, near Dolno Maalo or the old village as we call it, and there is the new part towards Radisani, the Rastak road. This is the new part of the village. They're now changes to the village. The houses may be more densely built up, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about what you saw in 2001, okay? And most houses are walled, aren't they? There are walls, high walls surrounding the homes in 2001 in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say again, high walls, they can't put up a palace wall. It's a normal wall, so the neighbour's cattle can't jump over.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I think you have answered my question. And there were lots of trees. It's a forested area, Ljuboten, is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending in which area of Ljuboten you're asking me about. Ljuboten is a more general and broader term and somewhat different now. Ljuboten, in that area towards the river. This is where it is. There are high poplar trees.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are trees, 100-year-old trees.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm only asking you about the area that you were -- that you saw while you were at Smok in August of 2001, okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go to Exhibit 2D97, please, and show that in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now we see there, sir, just by way of example, the houses that are built surrounding the mosque area and towards the area where the Orthodox church was located. That's a pretty densely built-up area, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the church. I can see the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But just what you're looking at right here, just by way of an example, around the mosque, the houses are quite close together, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same thing again. In the area of Dolno Maalo, the houses are closest and closer together. In the area towards the Rastak road, this is different. We're talking about the old Maalo now. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that's what I'm asking about. I'm not asking you about Rastak road. Now, at the time, sir, when you were making your observations from Smok between 10 and 12th of August, 2001, you didn't see any trenches or bunkers or any type of fortifications or sandbags in the village of Ljuboten, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th of August? Can you please ask the question again? You're asking me about where I was on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No sir. Let me just repeat that. We know you were in Smok on the 12th of August. What I'm asking you is when you were there --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: -- on the 10th and 12th of August, you did not see any sandbags, trenches, or bunkers or that type of fortification inside the village of Ljuboten, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I appreciate that sometimes you may have said things before, but I just need to clarify with them so bear with me if I have to ask you again, okay? Now when you were in Ljuboten, sir, on the 12th of August, and we're just dealing with the 12th right now, if I can ask you to please look at the screen, which is Exhibit 2D97, were you able to see, or did you see a group of police officers walking down the road to the left of the mosque and stop off at a couple of the houses along that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw I told you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you a different question, sir, and I know that you've told us other things but it's my job to ask you some other questions and sometimes things may seem obvious but I would just ask you to please answer my questions as I ask them. We can get through it faster, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw I told already.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So I take it then that your answer is no, you did not see police officers walking down the road to the left of the mosque in that densely populated area and stop off at a couple of houses. Your answer is no; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area which I'm not able to see here, from the church towards Dolno Maalo, I said in this area which could not have been seen, I could not have seen anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- why I told you who and what I saw and in what period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I take it then, sir, that you did not see that same group of officers go into one of these houses, round up about 15 or 20 men, force them to lie outside at the front gate and beat them. You did not see that, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that I saw something when I didn't see anything. That they were beating someone or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw, I already told you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And you did not see, sir -- sir, I'm asking you now a different question. You did not see, for example, the police shoot one of the men who got up and shoot another one who was still lying down in the front -- at the front of the gate of one of those houses, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tell me about which precise area and then I will give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We're still --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the area which is out of sight --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: We're still talking about the houses to the left of the mosque along the road. You have explained to us that you haven't seen this, sir; I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's a misunderstanding here but I have to intervene, Your Honours. In concrete terms, I told you what I saw. You speak about left from the mosques. What is the time that I saw the security forces from there towards the Rastak road? My point is that I've told this Court what I saw and when.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And sometimes, sir, part of the reason that you may not have seen certain things, is because your view was not only obstructed by the density of the village, because of the houses that were built closely together, but sometimes there was an embankment or walls or forested area that obstructed your view. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Houses are houses, movement is movement. What I saw I told you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I know that you've told me what you saw, but I'm asking you different questions now and I would like you, if you can please answer the question that I'm asking you. And sometimes if you didn't see something, you can just say no. You don't have to explain it again, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So, sir, would it be fair to say that you could not see inside the yards -- I'm sorry, are you having -- Are you able to hear me, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can you repeat the question though.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. It's fair to say then, sir, that you were not able to see inside the yards of the houses.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say what was in the yard. If I saw or took notes. And yesterday what I said before this Court was what I saw. In combat activities, depending on the given situation, I will say what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay, sir. So the answer then is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can then please turn to tab -- actually, I haven't distributed the binders and I will distribute them now, Your Honours, if I may. Perhaps if I can ask -- if we can show in the meantime tab P239 -- or, rather, Exhibit P239, and it's at tab 39 of the binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I take it then, sir, if you look at the photograph that is on the screen in front of you, that you did not see the body of that man, or that man get shot who is lying there behind that embankment. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I hadn't seen him, how could I say -- I hate injustice.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hate something that is inhuman.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Please, I'm asking you to just answer my questions, and they require yes or no answers, okay? And it is quite difficult to see at that angle because of the raised embankment. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pardon? Could you say it again, because ...

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It would be difficult for you to see from the position of Smok where you were located, that man, or shooting occur at that -- that location, because of the raised embankment. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, again, what I saw I said already before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, that wasn't my --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had seen him I would have told you that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. You've answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if I could then ask perhaps on -- if we can turn to 65 ter 195, which is at tab 36 in the binders, but in e-court it's 65 ter 195, N003-0029. And for the record, Your Honour, this photograph depicts the same image as in photograph P186.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you a question and you just have to answer yes or no, please. I take it you didn't see the shooting of this man that is depicted in the image that you see on your screen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I didn't see this man.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From where -- near some house, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. So it would be fair to say, sir, that there was a lot that happened or that was going on in the village that you may simply have not have seen, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to clarify this, Your Honours. What I saw from my position, I swore here that I would be telling the truth. What I saw is what I said and what I know. I wasn't down there to know everything that was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please go to Exhibit 2D98.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Actually, before -- before we do that ... This is an exhibit from -- that was admitted yesterday by my friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you said, sir, in looking at this image you drew two circles there, number 1 and 2, and you said that you saw the police officers walk down the road towards the cemetery behind a Hermelin. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the road, to the cemetery? No. Let me correct you. The Rastak road.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And these two points that I identified I already spoke about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you did see the police officers walking down that road behind a Hermelin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is what I saw. I told you how they were moving, how everything was going on. I said everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. You just have to answer yes or no to these questions, sir. And you also said that you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay? You also said that you saw five men fleeing from one of those houses wearing black uniforms. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That is exactly the number that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now my question to you, sir, is: Were they all wearing black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes before this trial. I emphasized it because I saw them. They were wearing weapons. I saw the gun falling down off one person's shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you about the weapons. I am just asking you about the uniforms now. All of them were wearing black uniforms. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also said that they were shot at by members of your unit while you were up in Smok. Do you recall telling us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said we were shooting from our positions, from Smok, and from Bomba as well, and I already spoke about it before this Court. But, yes, we shot. We were firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you also see the police fire at those persons, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly what I said yesterday. I cannot say something that is not true. I said as well that the police were shooting. I cannot say that they were not shooting. Everything I saw I said before this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You also said, sir, that you didn't see a weapon at the time until after one of them fell over and he fell on his weapon. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I explained it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Just requires a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, Ljuboten was a very -- a populated area at the time. There were lots of civilians, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said civilians. But we have to have in mind what I said. From this period to this period, the population, the villagers, were leaving the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But it would be fair to say, sir, that as far as you knew at the time, there were still people in the village who had not left on the 12th of August, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that, Your Honours. I cannot make things up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said what date --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All have you to do is answer yes or no to these questions and if you need to explain, it's fine. But if you have said something before --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So there were, so I can clarify this for the record, that there were still people in the village on the 12th of August, yes or no, civilians.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe so. There were elderly people. I said before this trial what I know. I cannot lie.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. So it's fair then to say, sir, that you and members of your unit had to be pretty careful not to fire at civilians, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. How can I shoot at civilians? Only a lunatic can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, sir, a combatant is normally one that would wear a uniform, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Combatant, soldiers. Our security forces, which are in the army, for example, there is an army procedure, an army law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir. Sir, the question was a very simple one. I didn't ask you about your security forces. I'm just saying normally one way to identify a combatant is someone who is wearing a uniform, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the uniform means that person is under some command.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you would expect, sir, that a combatant who is in the village would hide and take cover because he might be afraid that someone, such as yourself, may get him in your sights and take a shot at him. Wouldn't that be fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the situation. If it is with a mortar that is firing on the position, it's normal that every person is afraid. The question is are soldiers afraid? Every human beings are afraid because fire weapons because were used.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, it is pretty unlikely then, sir, that a combatant would run across an open field and risk being shot at by someone, such as yourself, who might be hiding up in the hills. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything is combat activity. As I said, from one foothill or one slope, if a person can take shelter, of course. If a person takes shelter, they can fire. But everything depends on the situation and on the direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to tab 41, 65 ter 989, please. If we can show that, display that on the e-court screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see that person there, sir, lying in the open field?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish I can have a clear picture that I can speak about. Maybe the person is just lying in this ditch and I couldn't see --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I'm only asking you if you see it now on your screen, okay? That's all I'm asking you. Okay. He doesn't look like he is wearing a black uniform, does he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looks like he's wearing a T-shirt. There are all kinds of T-shirt. Colourful, one-colour T-shirt --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: He doesn't look like a combatant to you, does he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looks as though he was wearing pyjamas to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened that they would change their clothes, combatants or no combatants.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, this is the same image as Exhibit P203, N000-7282. If we can then please turn to tab 32, 65 ter 195, N003-0033.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if you can look at your screen, sir. Once again, he doesn't look like he's wearing a uniform, does he? It's a very simple question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said if the person is change -- that is, if the person has changed his clothes or not, how I am supposed to see it?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe the person could have been brought here in pyjamas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you're speculating now, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not speculating. There's no need for me to speculate. He is wearing dark clothes. How can I say that he is wearing white shirt?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir that's not what I'm asking you, okay? I'm asking you to please listen to my questions and answer them as they're being asked.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And for the record, Your Honour, this photograph is the same image as Exhibit P203, N003-7827. I just didn't want to show the markings made by another protected witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to tab 10, P306, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've told us that the commander of your company was Commander Jurisic. This is a report that was written by Commander Jurisic regarding the events that occurred on the 12th of August, 2001, in the village of Ljuboten. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now I'd like to draw your attention, sir, to about the very last paragraph in this report that starts with: "At about 11.00," or 1100 hours. And what is say there, sir, is: "At about 1100 hours, our positions came under fire of 82-millimetre mortars and during this the grenades were falling at our positions. We realised that the fire was coming from the small forest near the village. After being ordered, the deputy fired five projectiles against the positions of the mortars of the terrorist groups, and after the fifth grenade the attack stopped." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report of Lieutenant Brasnarski. That is his statement, not mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: This is a report of, actually, Commander Jurisic, sir, and I appreciate it's not your statement. But there's nothing in here, sir, there's no reference to any so-called terrorists coming from the houses near the Rastak area and being fired upon by the army, is there? Very simple question, requires a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give this statement, and I cannot say yes. Whoever gave this statement is the person that said yes or no. No, I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: There's no reference here, sir, to the five terrorists that were wearing black uniforms that you say you saw, is there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is what I saw. But when and how Brasnarski decided and what kind of statement he gave, it's his statement. And this is my statement, and I cannot change it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you saw all of these events that you described to us, these events were reported to the command, whether it was by yourself or Brasnarski. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he said that he made a report, then it's true. This is his statement. I'm now talking about what I said to this trial and to this Chamber, and I'm standing behind it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we can then please turn to tab 12, 1D26.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And once again, sir, if I can just ask you to perhaps look at the binder in front of you, or -- or the screen, whatever is easier. If you look at the very bottom of this report, which is Lieutenant Brasnarski's report, it starts with: "At 1100 the terrorists opened mortar fire," and it continues. And once again there, sir, there's nothing in there about five terrorists wearing black uniforms fleeing and being shot at by the army, is there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is his statement. Your Honours, again, I have to say this. What I saw personally from my position is what I said before this Chamber. I cannot speak about the report that was given to -- from Brasnarski or what year it was given. I came here to speak before this Chamber about things that I saw and I'm standing behind what I say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the 10th of August, you testified that there were shootings from the Dolno Maalo area, which is near the church, as I understand it, and also you said that there were shootings or firing at your positions from the houses near the mosque and from the Rastanski Pat area. Do you recall telling us that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember what I said. I remember and I say yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. I noticed, sir, that you didn't mark on a photograph the precise location from where you say you saw the firing was coming from on the 10th of August. Is that because you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw, I spoke about it precisely. I cannot make up things or draw houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm not asking you, sir, to make up things. I'm asking you another question, and I'd like to you please carefully listen to what I'm asking you and to answer only that question. And what I'm asking you is you did not draw or you did not mark on any photograph the precise location of where you say you saw the firing was coming from on the 10th of August. Is that because you don't recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well and I said it before this Chamber. What I marked is the fact reflecting what I saw. I cannot now make up things. Maybe some new 50 houses were built on those locations. What I recognised on the monitor is what I --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm interrupting you again because you're not listening to my question. I am only talking about the 10th of August right now. What you marked related to the 12th of August. I'm asking you about the 10th of August, okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now you said, sir, that on the 10th of August you and your unit or the army, fired with your sniper and automatic weapons at those targets that evening. Do you recall telling us that? It require a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said in the evening. No, we were not shooting in the evening. We were shoots against targets from where shots were fired at us. No, I don't agree it was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it wasn't in the evening but you fired with your sniper and automatic weapons, that's what you said, at those targets, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, what I said precisely before I will say it again. We were shooting from our position with weapons. I couldn't make it up. Yes, it's true we were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Didn't you also, sir, fire mortars at the village or shell the village on the 10th of August, in addition to firing with your infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I emphasize that I spoke from which position and -- yes, that is my answer. Yes, we were shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You fired mortars on the 10th of August at the village, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Was it 10th of August or other day? What I said I would like to confirm. I stand behind what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm asking you, sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said when we were firing against what targets we were firing. I said it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would like to you listen very carefully to my question, sir, okay? On the 10th of August, isn't it true that your units, or the army, other units in the army, fired mortars or shells at the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said what I said and I stand behind it. I cannot fabricate things about the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I am asking to you answer my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I answered it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You did not --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You did. Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you're listening to me. Everything that I spoke about and what happened on the 10th of August, I spoke and I confirmed facts. How can I say that we were not firing when we were firing. I stand behind what I said. I'm a witness here, aren't I?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And isn't it true, sir, that on the 10th of August a child was killed by the shelling of the village that your units were firing at the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that. Maybe a child was killed. I couldn't say it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, did you report the fact that your positions were being fired upon from the village on the 10th of August to your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the commander that is on that position, he is the person that reports, and he reports to the commanding post. He's the person that reports on the fires -- firing, where the firing comes from and reports this information to the command centre, and I precisely said who was the person that was commander-in-chief and who was the person that was reporting the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: On that day, sir, it was Commander Brasnarski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the reason, sir, as far as you know or you understand that the commander, whether it be the commander at the position or some other commander, reports back is ultimately -- that information makes it up to the battalion commander. The information -- or the observations or the information that is received at Smok ultimately goes back to the command centre and makes it to the battalion commander. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a military expert. I don't know this commanding stuff. I'm an ordinary soldier, a peasant. Whether information arrived in the commanding centre and from where, I wouldn't know. What I said is what I stand behind. Brasnarski, what he said and what his report was about, I already spoke about this briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir. But even as an ordinary soldier, or ordinary reservist, you know that you give information to your immediate commander and then that commander passes that information to his commander and then it makes its way up the chain of command to the ultimate commander. Isn't that the way it works in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm not the person --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I would just like to turn to tab 29, which is Exhibit P301.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now I appreciate, sir, that this is not your report. It's the report of Major Despodov who was the battalion commander. But if I can ask you to have a look at that report, either on your screen or in the binder in front of you. And specifically if I can ask you to have a look at the second page of the report, you would agree with me, sir, that there's nothing in the report that refers to your positions being fired at from the village of Ljuboten, is there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whose this is. You say this is of the commander. This is their statement. I didn't give any statements like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir. I'm simply asking you to look at the report. I know you didn't give the statement and there's nothing in that report that refers to shootings coming from within the village. Just requires a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not write this so I cannot respond neither yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I take it, sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot respond to this. I absolutely don't agree. I have not given this statement. I don't know who wrote this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies for interrupting, Your Honours. But it would be fair to have the first page read out to the witness as well, not just the last passage, so that the witness can hear this page being read out loud to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I suspect that there will be no value in doing that given his very firmly expressed attitude to the whole report. Thank you, though, Mr. Apostolski. At a convenient point we will break. You tell me when you think it is convenient, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: It's actually convenient now, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the first break now, resuming at 20 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'd like you to please turn, with the assistance of Madam Usher, to tab 9 of your binder, which is P305, the war diary of the 3rd Guardist Battalion, and I'm going to page N001-4734. And I will read out to you the portions that I'm referring to. And on the date of the 10th of August, 2001, the war diary, which describes the events that took place on that date, says: "In the area of Basinec at about 7.45 in the morning, a vehicle of the 2nd Company had hit two explosive devices, planted by terrorists in ambush while bringing soldiers on a regular shift at the check-point Zdravec, on the way back. During this, seven soldiers were killed and one soldier, later at the military hospital in Skopje. We fired with all our weapons to the ambush, as well as with artillery weapons. After three hours of fight, we smashed the terrorist group and they withdrew towards Jesmenica and Bacila, whereas a part of the group was noticed as they withdrew towards Ljuboten village and we fired on them." Now, that's the entry, sir, in its entirety that refers to the 10th of August 2001, and I'm just going to put it to you again and ask you to answer yes or no, there's no reference in the war diary of that date of firing from within the village as you had described earlier, is there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who made this log? I don't know this, and therefore I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: The question is simple, sir. There is no reference in what I read out to that -- to what you described earlier as firing coming from within the village. I'm not asking you about who made this log and what you can say. There's just nothing in there that refers to that, is there? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I knew I said about the shooting, and this is written in the command and everywhere. I said this very precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I know what you've said. I'm asking you a different question now. And I would ask you - we're almost at the end of the examination - to please answer the questions as I ask them, not repeat what you've said earlier. Yesterday, sir, you testified that on the 11th of August you left your position at Smok and attended the funeral of those reservists who were killed in the Ljubotenski Bacila mining incident. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did others in your unit also leave their position at Smok and attend the funeral?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part. What I said already was very precise. Some of us from the village who requested to go, there were 100 soldiers from the village, those from the village of Ljubanci, we asked of the commander to give us leave to go to the funeral. So my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If there was a barrage of firing against your position, sir, as you described occurred the day before, how is it that you and others could leave your positions to attend the funeral in Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very precisely, on the 11th, on Saturday, we asked the commander that we go to the funeral, and he gave us leave and we attended the funeral in Ljubanci. This was very precisely said.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Wasn't there a concern, sir, that firing against your positions would continue on the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was concern but I cannot attest to this, because I wasn't on the position on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You said, sir, that you were very upset by the tragedy and had trouble sleeping that night and presumably the men in your unit were also very upset after the explosion on the 10th of August. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, are you still upset by that tragedy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will be upset by this as long as I live. I cannot forget that picture just like that. This is a tragedy that happened. It's something that drives me still to jump up in the middle of the night but this is not something for me to say here. This tragedy will remain with me as long as I'm alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you feel, sir, that you need to support the actions of the police by your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What support do you mean? You say the support. Our security forces. I always say this and I won't change this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you feel, sir, that you need to support the accused by your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to support them. What I knew I said, plain and clear, before this Chamber. I had no order to give such support, nor can I say who did what or why and how. They're experts who think about these things. I am a villager, a peasant soldier. I cannot issue commands, I cannot issue orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't ask you that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made this quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm going to put to you a couple of propositions now, sir, and I'm going to ask you if you agree or you disagree or you don't know. And the questions that I'm going to put to you only require the answers, yes, no, or I don't know. Okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I put it to you, sir, that on the 12th of August, the police went into a number of houses and either beat or killed the men in those houses who were unarmed civilians. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot agree with this when I did not see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I put it to you, sir, that you either did not see the illegal activity of the police or you're not being entirely candid or truthful about your observations on the 12th of August. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, cannot agree with this. I have been sincere and truthful and honest. I'm not making anything up. I cannot say something that I've made up. Honesty to me is a very important thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think you've answered my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Issa. Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the purpose of the transcript I would like to say that I did not and do not have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understood the questions were asked by you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, this was the case with the other witness. Perhaps I omitted to say this before my learned colleague began her cross-examination. So I just wanted to make this comment for the purpose of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it is my failing, and I'm very sorry and apologise if you were not called on. I regret that, I'm sorry. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I will just have a few more questions for you. Do you recall when the Prosecutor asked you today, saying that a combatant is someone who is wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is a person to you, someone who is wearing civilian clothing and a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A combatant of some sort. Since he is carrying weapons, it must be a combatant.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P203, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You can see this on the screen, Witness. Can you see the colour of the clothing of this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dark colour. What other colour can I say?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If the jacket of this person were to be zipped up, and if you are looking at this person from the position where you're at, what would this person look like to you? What colour would this seem to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Black, of course. How can I say otherwise? How can I say white when it's black?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In that period, a marking of the NLA, was said to be black clothing. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. They were wearing black T-shirts, black uniforms. I can't make up something and say that they were wearing brown. I said this quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could now the witness be shown page 3 of the same exhibit, P203.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell how this person is dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph turned towards the sun, but I can see that it is a dark colour, that it's not yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the purpose of the transcript, I would like to say that these are the victims Kadri Jashari and Bajram Jashari. Can the witness now please be shown 2D64.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see two pictures in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The picture to the right --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: -- there's a person with a number 12 next to him and a person standing next to this person. Can you tell us how this person is dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person on the right is dressed in black.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What does he have on his feet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What does he hold in his hand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Black Arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is a Black Arrow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a weapon with a range of 10.000 metres, 5.000 metres is a precise firing range.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can the witness please be shown 2D67. Can we see the photograph on the right, and to enlarge it?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see this photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see how the persons on this photograph are dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They're dressed differently. I cannot see quite well on this picture. They're dressed differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now go to 2D56.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person marked with the number 5?
