utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us who this is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is their commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is his name? If you know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment I'm very excited. He is in the parliament now. His name escapes me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Do you see the person with the number 7 and what -- and the colour of his clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: What is the colour of his clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M2D-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Black.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will be pleased to know, sir, that that concludes the questions for you. We would thank you for your attendance here in The Hague and you will now be able to return to your home and your normal activities, and the court officer will now show you out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, are there any procedural matters that can be dealt with at this point while we have some time? Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, with respect to the matter of translations, I would like to put on the record that a Macedonian translation of Exhibit P00494 has now been linked to the original English version. This exhibit is a report from the international crisis group Macedonia, the last chance for peace, and the -- it is ERN MT-N002-5224 to 5245. And in addition, Your Honour, a Macedonian translation of Exhibit P00298 has now been linked on e-court. This was a map of the Ljuboten area, indicating positions of Macedonian security forces. Moving to another topic, Your Honour, you may recall that on the 6th of November of last year, Your Honour instructed myself and Mr. Mettraux to meet and discuss what is Exhibit 1D00229 and come to an agreement as to which pages of that lengthy document should be admitted into evidence, and this is at page 7383 to 7384 of the transcript. And I'm pleased to report that, myself and Mr. Mettraux, we have come to an agreement and the pages that should be -- And, Your Honours, if you allow me I will simply read into the record the pages that should be treated as admitted. The first would be a report from Butan 1, dated 8th of August, 2001, bearing the ERN range 1D00-7278-1D00-7279. The second portion would be a Butan 1 report, dated the 10th of August, 2001, bears ERN number 1D00-7281. The third portion is a Butan 1 report, dated the 23rd of August, 2001, bearing ERN number 1D00-7301-1D00-7304. And lastly, Your Honour, a Butan 1 report dated 9th of August, 2001, bearing ERN range 1D00-7279-1D00-7280. I don't know if my colleague wants to make any comment about this or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour. I think that Mr. Saxon was correct to the extent that we have agreed to the material that had been used to be tendered at this stage by the Prosecution. We do believe, however, that we had indicated to Mr. Saxon, and I apologise if that was misunderstood, but that we had in fact reservation about the admission of one such report which is the one from the 23rd of August of 2001 which is 1D00-7301-1D00-7304. The reason for it, Your Honour, was the indication given by the Chamber at the time that only those parts of the report which had actually been used or shown to a particular witness should be tendered by the parties. And this is our understanding, that this particular report was not used or not shown to any particular witness, and I would stand corrected if Mr. Saxon believes that this is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, when Mr. Mettraux and I had spoken about this matter and I went back and checked the records regarding the pages which the Prosecution wished to admit, I realised that I had suggested a particular ERN range which, indeed, the Prosecution had not used and so I have admitted to put that ERN range in the record. I could be wrong. It had been my understanding that the Butan 1 report from 23 August 2001, bearing the ERN range 1D00-7301-1D00-7304, was actually a portion of this document that the Defence wished to tender. If I am wrong about that, I am perfectly happy to retract those pages as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Mr. Saxon, Your Honour. I believe we have tendered those parts of the larger document that we wished to tender and I believe that was not one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't understand that last comment because I thought that we had been told to come to an agreement as to which parts of the documents we were going to tender, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps for clarification sake, Your Honour, we have sought to tender in one of our bar table motion a number of section of that same documents. And this particular part of the report that Mr. Saxon just read was not one of them, so we haven't sought to tender this part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You mean you're prepared to run the risk of not having any part of this admitted on the bar table motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we believe that pursuant to your own indications we had limited application for admission to those part which had been used which would mean that this particular part was not sought to be tendered by the Defence for this reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we seem to have no agreement in this agreement. So you're happy to withdraw the 23rd of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. That will not be received. By consent, the other three reports that have been identified by Mr. Saxon, will now comprise Exhibit 1D239.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, that should be Exhibit 1D229.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A very helpful suggestion from the registry officer, this exhibit will be 1D229.1, so that the whole report will remain as -- or the whole bundle will remain marked for identification, which will ensure, among other things, that we are in a position to deal with Mr. Mettraux's motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I raise one more brief matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Although I fear that I may be sounding like a broken record or a broken CD now, I have the sad duty to inform the Chamber that the Prosecution team is losing yet another member of its -- of its team. Ms. Issa has been called back to her office with the Crown Prosecutor's department in Toronto and she will soon be leaving the Tribunal, and so you may not see her again after today. And I would just like to extend my thanks to Ms. Issa for the fine contributions that she has made to the work of the Prosecution and to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I think we have had reason to comment in the past on the frequency with which news such as this has had to be given to us by you. We appreciate the difficulty that has created for you and those assisting you. For Ms. Issa, it has been a short stay here, and we would wish you well as you return to your duties in Canada, and thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any other matter? That being so, we will now adjourn for the day. I thank counsel for their assistance in ensuring that we did not waste time. We resume on Monday in the morning. I have to attend a ceremony shortly before 9.00 on Monday for the swearing in of another Judge, and it may be that I will be a few minutes late. Subject to that, we will adjourn until 9.00 a.m. on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 10th day of March, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
